spec.name: arx_chain_periodic_v1
spec.limitations: The key is 16 bits, so one known plaintext/ciphertext pair allows an exhaustive search over at most 65,536 keys that recovers the key and opens any other message under it; the construction has no strength beyond that key space. The key schedule repeats with period 2, so positions i and i+2 always use the same key byte, and the chain steps may expose repeated additive structure on long messages. Rotation amounts and public constants are fixed and public, so this is one fixed permutation family; differential and linear behaviour and chain-step trails are not analysed here. Toy construction, not a vetted cipher.
spec.math: Let the message be x in (Z/256)^n and let the 16-bit key be two bytes k0,k1 with K_i = k_{i mod 2}. Every step is a bijection of (Z/256)^n: per-byte steps are x_i -> x_i xor K_i, x_i -> x_i + K_i mod 256, x_i -> x_i xor c, x_i -> x_i + c mod 256, x_i -> ROL(x_i,r); chain_add is y_i = x_i + y_{i-1} mod 256 with y_{-1}=0, i.e. a unit lower-triangular all-ones matrix over Z/256; chain_xor is y_i = x_i xor y_{i-1} with y_{-1}=0, a unit lower-triangular GF(2)-linear map. The composite is a bijection for every key; its inverse is the step list reversed with each step replaced by its inverse: same xor/add constant or key byte, ROL(r) -> ROR(r), chain_add -> x_i = y_i - y_{i-1}, chain_xor -> x_i = y_i xor y_{i-1}.
spec.assumptions: Assumes the engine substitutes the real key byte for each *_key operand and ignores the placeholder; chain_add and chain_xor start from an implicit previous byte of 0 at position 0; rol n is an 8-bit left rotation; decryption runs the reversed program with the same 16-bit key; the adversary knows the program and public constants plus any known plaintext/ciphertext pairs, but not the key.
